stories.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon to developers
stories.summary: Gemini 4 Argon is out globally via the Gemini API in AI Studio at an introductory $2/$10 per million input/output tokens (rising to $4/$20 after Nov 30, 2026), with a 1M unified input-output token limit; Google says it lifted agentic code submissions in Antigravity by more than 35%.
stories.why: A new frontier model priced for API builders is directly usable in the LLM pipelines and agents he builds.

stories.title: Liquid AI releases open-weight LFM2.5-24B-A2B for on-device agents
stories.summary: The 24B-parameter model uses 2B active parameters, has a 131,072-token context, scores 27.69 on AutomationBench versus 8.72 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and ships open-weight on Hugging Face with API pricing of $0.10/$1.00 per million input/output tokens.
stories.why: A cheap open model tuned for tool calling and automation fits n8n-style workflows that need to run locally or at low cost.

stories.title: Nairobi founder's Startup Map Hub helps founders find and apply for funding
stories.summary: Launched in October 2025 by Nairobi software engineer Duncan Muriithi, Startup Map Hub has 2,415 registered founders, at least 35 paying, and over $2,000 in revenue since it began charging in February 2026.
stories.why: A small Nairobi-built AI-assisted product, the kind of early-stage local team that hires generalist engineers.

stories.title: African VCs say AI startups need moats beyond the model
stories.summary: Investors from TLcom, Madica, Village Capital and others say they now pay for local-language voice, deep customer integration, licences and revenue; TechCabal Insights counted 207 African AI startups across 17 countries in 2025, up from 104 in 2022.
stories.why: Shows where African AI money is going: integration-heavy products, which matches his integrations-and-LLM profile.

stories.title: Infinite Partners closes $169.3 million South African fund
stories.summary: The mid-market private equity firm raised R2.8 billion ($169.3 million) for Core Equity Fund II, above its R2.5 billion target, with first investments in enterprise software firm e4 and digital infrastructure business CYNK.
stories.why: More capital for tech-enabled African businesses such as enterprise software can mean more engineering hiring across the region.

stories.title: Microsoft winding down its Nairobi Africa Development Centre
stories.summary: TechCabal reports nearly 400 jobs at risk at the ADC in Westlands, with staff told to meet managers by Friday, October 16, on exit options; Microsoft said it is "communicating directly with employees in Kenya about proposed changes" but did not confirm the closure.
stories.why: Hundreds of experienced Nairobi engineers may enter the local job market at once, raising competition for the roles he is targeting.

stories.title: Bending Spoons lays off Airtable staff a month after buying it
stories.summary: Bending Spoons says the layoffs include a "large part" of the Airtable team, one month after the acquisition.
stories.why: Acquisition-driven cuts keep adding experienced engineers to the remote job pool he is competing in.

stories.title: CBK seeks powers to take over struggling payment firms
stories.summary: The draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 would let the Central Bank of Kenya intervene in a payment provider that fails its obligations to customers, appoint a statutory manager to sell the business and remove officials it holds responsible.
stories.why: Tighter oversight of Kenyan payment fintechs shapes how firms like Kwara build compliance into their products.

stories.title: Safaricom launches Ziidi Shari'ah fund inside M-PESA
stories.summary: The Shari'ah-compliant money market fund, run with GulfCap Investment Bank and regulated by the CMA, allows free deposits and withdrawals from M-PESA, subject to the KES 250,000 per-transaction and KES 500,000 daily limits.
stories.why: M-PESA keeps moving into savings and investing, a growing area for Kenyan fintech engineering work.

stories.title: Safaricom says M-PESA limits are set by CBK
stories.summary: Replying to a customer's call for a Ksh10 million limit, Safaricom said on X that mobile money limits are regulated by CBK; the limits stay at Ksh250,000 per transaction, Ksh500,000 a day and Ksh500,000 account balance.
stories.why: Transaction caps are a constraint any M-PESA integration he builds has to handle.
